body.heading: Choose your pattern
paragraphs: A pattern is something that repeats in order. Choose a colour pattern for your chain — red, blue, red, blue is the simplest. Red, red, blue is trickier.
Lay your strips out in pattern order before you glue anything. Planning first saves unpicking later.

body.heading: Loop and glue
paragraphs: Curl the first strip into a loop and glue the ends. Thread the next strip through the loop before gluing it. Your chain grows link by link.
Check your pattern as you go. If a wrong colour sneaks in, your chain will tell the story — and mistakes can be unglued or kept as surprises.

body.heading: How long can it grow?
paragraphs: Count your links. Ten? Twenty? A chain long enough to cross the whole room is a family project.
Patterns are everywhere once you start looking — in chains, in songs, in days of the week. You built one with your own hands.

takeaway: A paper chain built in a colour pattern turns repeating order into something you can hold.
safetyNotes: An adult should help with cutting the strips. Glue sticks only — no hot glue.
screenFreeExtension: Hang your chain and read its pattern out loud like a song: red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue.
